questions.question: After sorting the points by X-coordinate, what is the immediate next step in the Divide and Conquer Closest Pair algorithm?

answers.b: Divide the set into left and right halves

explanations.a: That would revert to brute force.
explanations.b: The sorted set is split into two spatial halves using the median X value.
explanations.c: Y-sorting is done later for strip optimization.
explanations.d: The strip is created only after recursive distances are computed.

questions.question: If the minimum distances from left and right halves are δL = 5 and δR = 3, what is the value of δ used for the strip?
What condition determines whether a point is included in the vertical strip?

explanations.b: Points within δ distance from the dividing line are included.
explanations.c: Y-distance is not used for strip selection.
explanations.d: Centroid is not used in the algorithm.

questions.question: Why does the algorithm sort strip points by Y-coordinate?

answers.b: To ensure faster drawing of points
answers.c: To limit distance comparisons to nearby vertical neighbors

explanations.a: Sorting does not change recursion depth.
explanations.c: Y-sorting ensures each point is compared only with nearby points.
explanations.d: Centroid is not part of the algorithm.

questions.question: Which input distribution causes maximum strip density and worst-case behavior?

explanations.b: Collinear points place many points near the division line.
explanations.d: Circular distribution does not concentrate near median.

questions.question: Which case represents the best-case behavior for the Divide and Conquer algorithm?
Why does Divide and Conquer outperform brute force for large n?

answers.b: It avoids computing unnecessary distance pairs

questions.question: If the strip contains no points, what is the final closest pair result?

answers.c: The minimum of left and right recursive results

explanations.c: If strip is empty, cross-pairs are impossible.

questions.question: Which stage of the algorithm is responsible for reducing time complexity from O(n²) to O(n log n)?

explanations.b: Sorting alone is O(n log n) but not sufficient.
explanations.d: Recursion without pruning still leads to n².
